title: Revision and Exam Technique
description: High-yield review of the whole course plus the exam skills that convert knowledge into marks.
objectives: Recall the highest-yield facts from every module
Handle data, graph and timing pressure

topics.title: High-Yield Review
topics.description: The most-examined ideas from Modules 1–10, compressed and connected.

lessons.title: Cells to Genetics Express
lessons.description: One-pass review: life, cells, molecules, division and inheritance.
objectives: State the MRS GREN set, cell trio and transport trio
Reproduce the food-test colours and enzyme curves
Solve a monohybrid and a sex-linked cross from scratch
lessons.introduction: Five modules, one lesson: the facts that earn half the marks in any biology paper. Retrieve each from memory BEFORE reading on.

contents.title: The non-negotiables (Modules 1–5)
contents.body: MODULE 1: MRS GREN (all seven for life); cell = smallest living unit; five kingdoms by cell type/number/nutrition. MODULE 2: plant trio (wall, chloroplasts, big vacuole); prokaryote = no nucleus; diffusion (down gradient), osmosis (water + membrane), active transport (ATP, uphill); I = M × A. MODULE 3: starch/glycogen/cellulose roles; condensation out, hydrolysis in; enzyme curves (temperature cliff, pH optimum, substrate plateau); food colours — iodine blue-black (starch), Benedict's brick-red (sugar), biuret purple (protein), emulsion milky (fat). MODULE 4: PMAT + cytokinesis → 2 identical diploid; meiosis → 4 unique haploid; homologues part in anaphase I; variation = crossing over + assortment + random fertilisation. MODULE 5: five-step crosses; 3:1 and 1:2:1; ABO genotypes; X-linked males show single copies; normal parents + affected child = recessive. If any line above feels fuzzy, re-open that module NOW — Module 12 assumes mastery.

contents.title: Worked example: the chain question
contents.body: Question: 'Using cells, enzymes and genes, explain why a child with cystic fibrosis struggles to digest food.' (Chain across modules!) Step 1 — GENES (M5): the child is homozygous recessive for a faulty CFTR-channel allele. Step 2 — CELLS (M2): faulty channels trap chloride in cells; mucus dehydrates and thickens. Step 3 — ENZYMES (M3): thick mucus blocks pancreatic ducts, so lipase/trypsin never reach the gut — fats and proteins pass undigested. Step 4 — Conclude: one allele → broken transport → blocked enzymes → malnutrition. Examiners LOVE cross-module chains — practise building them: gene → protein → cell → system → symptom.

contents.title: Watch: Mega Genetics Review (again, actively)
contents.body: Rewatch 'Mega Genetics Review' by the Amoeba Sisters (official channel stream) — this time PAUSE before every solution and solve on paper. Active rewatching beats passive rereading.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
Retrieve before rereading: cover, recall, then check.
Colours, curves, ratios and equations must be WRITTEN from memory, not recognised.
Chain answers across modules: gene → protein → cell → system → symptom.
Revisit fuzzy modules immediately — gaps compound.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Modules 1–5 compress to: life's seven signs, cells' structures and traffic, molecules' colours and curves, divisions' precision and shuffling, and inheritance's ratios. Own them cold.

lessons.title: Ecology to Practicals Express
lessons.description: One-pass review: evolution, ecology, humans, plants and practical skills.
objectives: Recite selection steps, cycles and circulation traces
State microscope drill and fair-test rules
lessons.introduction: The second half of the course, same deal: retrieve first, read second. Ten modules down — finish the sweep.

contents.title: The non-negotiables (Modules 6–10)
contents.body: MODULE 6: selection = variation + competition + survival + inheritance; populations evolve; homologous (same build) vs analogous (same job); speciation = isolation → divergence → sterility. MODULE 7: arrows = energy flow; 10% transfers (respiration first); carbon in by photosynthesis, out by respiration/decay/combustion; nitrogen via Rhizobium → Nitrosomonas/Nitrobacter → plants → decay → denitrifiers; eutrophication chain; relationships scored +/−. MODULE 8: gut order + enzymes (amylase/pepsin/trypsin/lipase, bile emulsifies); heart trace (right=pulmonary, left=systemic, left ventricle thickest); breathe in = ribs up, diaphragm flat; aerobic ~30 ATP vs anaerobic ~2 + debt; insulin down/glucagon up; reflex arc five stations. MODULE 9: photosynthesis equation + five leaf adaptations + limiting factors; xylem up (transpiration pull), phloem any direction; germination = water + oxygen + warmth (no light). MODULE 10: microscope drill (low→high, fine-only); drawing rules (large, pencil, no shade, ruled labels); safety (goggles, water baths, report all); design (one IV, repeats, controls).

contents.title: Worked example: the synoptic chain
contents.body: Question: 'Explain how deforestation can raise global temperatures AND reduce rainfall.' Step 1 — CARBON (M7): fewer trees = less CO2 absorbed + burning releases stored carbon → stronger greenhouse effect → warming. Step 2 — WATER (M9): fewer leaves = less TRANSPIRATION → less atmospheric moisture → fewer clouds → less rain downwind (the flying-rivers effect). Step 3 — FEEDBACK: drought kills more trees → cycle worsens. One question, three modules (ecology, plants, cycles) — synoptic answers name each link explicitly. Practise spotting which modules a question raids.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
Second-half spine: selection steps, cycles, traces, equations, drills.
Synoptic questions raid 2–3 modules — name every link.
Deforestation links carbon AND water cycles — learn it as the model synoptic answer.
Teach-back test: explain each line aloud simply.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Modules 6–10 compress to mechanisms you can recite: selection, cycles, traces, equations and drills. Link them synoptically and no question can ambush you.

topics.title: Exam Technique
topics.description: Command words, marking logic, data questions and timing under pressure.

lessons.title: Command Words and Marking
lessons.description: What STATE, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN, EVALUATE and SUGGEST actually demand.
objectives: Respond correctly to six command words
Write to the mark allocation (points = marks)
lessons.introduction: Students lose 20% of marks knowing the biology but missing the COMMAND. Technique is free marks — collect them.

contents.title: The six commands
contents.body: STATE/GIVE/NAME (1 mark each): bare facts, no explanation — 'Name the bond joining amino acids' → 'peptide bond.' Full stop. DESCRIBE: say WHAT happens (patterns, sequences) — no reasons. 'Describe the temperature curve' → 'rises to 37°C then falls steeply.' EXPLAIN: say WHY — mechanisms required. 'Explain the fall' → 'heat denatures the enzyme; the active site loses shape.' COMPARE: similarities AND differences, paired point-by-point (use 'both... whereas...' — one-sided answers halve marks). EVALUATE/DISCUSS: strengths + weaknesses + judgement with evidence. SUGGEST: apply knowledge to NEW situations — reason from first principles aloud; there is no memorised answer. MARK MATHS: 3 marks = 3 distinct points (number them); 'explain' chains need because-links; never contradict yourself (examiners mark wrong science even beside right science).

contents.title: Five classic mark-losers
contents.body: (1) VAGUE AGENTS — 'it goes up the plant' (WHAT goes? water? sugar? name it). (2) MISSING COMPARISONS — describing one side of a compare question. (3) UNITS ABSENT — numbers without mm/°C/min bleed marks. (4) CONTRADICTIONS — 'diffusion needs no energy because ATP drives it' scores ZERO for the point. (5) ANSWERING ANOTHER QUESTION — restating the question's data instead of explaining it. Bonus time rule: minutes ≈ marks × 1.2 — a 5-mark question gets ~6 minutes, then MOVE ON; unfinished easy marks beat perfected hard ones. Always attempt everything: blank = zero, attempt ≥ zero.

contents.title: Worked example: describe vs explain
contents.body: Data: enzyme rate 10 (20°C), 25 (37°C), 2 (60°C). (a) DESCRIBE (2): 'Rate rises from 10 to 25 between 20–37°C, then falls sharply to 2 at 60°C.' — pattern + numbers, zero reasons. (b) EXPLAIN the fall from 37–60°C (2): 'Above the optimum, heat breaks the weak bonds holding the active site's tertiary shape (denaturation), so substrate no longer fits and few complexes form.' — mechanism + consequence. Notice: (a) with reasons wastes time; (b) without because-links scores 1 of 2. Match the command, count your points, stop.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
State = facts. Describe = what. Explain = why (because-links). Compare = both + whereas. Evaluate = pros + cons + judgement. Suggest = reason from principles.
Points = marks: number them. Never contradict. Units always.
Minutes ≈ marks × 1.2; attempt everything.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Commands are contracts: deliver exactly what each demands, in as many points as marks allow, with units and agents named. Technique turns B biology into A results.

references: WOLI DAN TECH HUB original — exam technique guide (WAEC/NECO/JAMB conventions)

lessons.title: Data Questions and Timing
lessons.description: Tables, graphs and practical scenarios — a systematic attack plan plus paper strategy.
objectives: Apply the READ-PLAN-ANSWER routine to data questions
Calculate percentages, means and rates correctly
lessons.introduction: Data questions panic students who memorised notes but never practised thinking. A routine replaces panic — read, plan, answer, check.

contents.title: The data routine
contents.body: READ (1 min): read the STEM fully — underline the IV, DV and units; study EVERY table row and axis before touching questions. PLAN (30 s): note which module each sub-question raids; jot the 2–3 points each mark needs. ANSWER: calculations show FORMULA → SUBSTITUTION → ANSWER + UNITS (method marks survive arithmetic slips); % change = (change ÷ original) × 100; means exclude ANOMALIES (circle and note them — never silently delete); rates = quantity ÷ time. GRAPHS: axes (IV-X, DV-Y, units), 3/4-page scales, small precise plots, best-fit line/curve, title. CHECK (last 5 min of paper): units, contradictions, unanswered parts, candidate details. PAPER STRATEGY: first pass — all confident questions; second pass — hard ones with fresh eyes; never leave blanks; if stuck >3 min, mark and move.

contents.title: Worked example: the full routine
contents.body: Table: light distance 10/20/30/40 cm → bubbles 42/24/11/6 per min. (a) Describe the trend (2): 'As distance increases from 10 to 40 cm, bubble rate falls steeply from 42 to 6 per minute — fastest drop between 10–20 cm.' (b) Explain using limiting factors (2): 'Greater distance lowers light intensity (limiting factor), slowing the light-dependent reactions, so less oxygen evolves per minute.' (c) Suggest why 10 cm might be anomalous-friendly (1): 'Lamp heat warms the tube — temperature confounds the light effect; a heat shield/water bath would control it.' Three sub-questions, three modules (M9 rate, M9 factors, M10 design) — the routine handles all.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
READ (IV/DV/units) → PLAN (modules, points) → ANSWER (formula-sub-answer-units) → CHECK.
% change, anomaly-circling means, rate = quantity/time.
Two passes: confident first, hard second. Blanks forbidden.
Stuck >3 min: mark, move, return.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Data questions yield to routine: read precisely, plan by module, calculate with shown working, check at the end. Two passes and zero blanks maximise every paper.

references: WOLI DAN TECH HUB original — data-question workbook (see practical)

practical.title: Timed Drill — 20 Questions in 25 Minutes
practical.objective: Practise full exam pace: read, calculate, write and move on under time pressure.
practical.scenario: Use any 20 quiz/exam questions you previously missed (or the module quizzes below) as your drill paper.
practical.instructions: 1. Collect 20 questions you got wrong before (or re-take Module 1–3 quizzes fresh). 2. Set a 25-minute timer, phone away, desk clear — exam conditions. 3. Answer in order; mark-and-move any question exceeding 90 seconds. 4. Mark harshly against the explanations (half-understood = wrong). 5. Log every miss in three columns: question | correct concept | WHY I missed it (knowledge/technique/panic). 6. Re-study the top 3 miss-reasons for 30 minutes, then re-attempt those questions untimed. SAFETY: none — but sleep properly; cramming past midnight destroys recall.
practical.expected_output: Score + miss-log table + 30-minute repair notes on top 3 reasons.
evaluation_criteria: Miss-log categorises every miss by reason
Repair notes show the corrected concepts in own words

assignment.title: Weakness Clinic Report
assignment.description: Diagnose your three weakest areas from module-exam history, re-study them, and prove the gains.
assignment.instructions: 1. List your scores on all module quizzes/exams taken so far (honest numbers). 2. Identify your THREE weakest topics (lowest scores or slowest answers). 3. For each: state the topic, quote one question you missed with YOUR wrong answer, explain the correct concept in your own words (100+ words each), and re-take that module's quiz — record old vs new score. 4. Build a 7-day revision timetable (topics × days × minutes) targeting the weaknesses first. 5. Submit scores table + three repairs + timetable (450–550 words plus tables).
assignment.requirements: Real scores from your attempts; invented gains are obvious and score zero.
assignment.expected_output: Score history + 3 concept repairs with re-take evidence + 7-day timetable.
evaluation_criteria: Honest score history with correctly identified weakest three
Each repair explains the concept accurately in own words with re-take evidence
Timetable is specific, weakness-first and realistic

questions.question: Which is found in plant cells but not animal cells?
questions.explanation: The large permanent vacuole (with wall and chloroplasts) is plant-only. The rest occur in both.

questions.question: Biuret solution turns purple in the presence of:
questions.explanation: Purple/violet with biuret = protein. (Starch: iodine blue-black. Sugar: Benedict's brick-red.)

questions.question: Sister chromatids separate during:
questions.explanation: Anaphase (mitosis and meiosis II). In meiosis I, whole homologues separate instead.

questions.question: A couple are both carriers (Aa) for a recessive condition. The probability of an affected child is:
questions.explanation: Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, Aa, aa — 1 in 4 affected (aa).

questions.question: 'Explain' as a command word requires you to:
questions.explanation: Explain = WHY. Describe = WHAT. State = bare facts. Match the command to earn full marks.

assessment.title: Module 11 Examination — Mixed Review
assessment.description: Mixed examination across Modules 6–10 plus technique.
assessment.instructions: Answer ALL 6 questions in 25 minutes. Pass mark is 60%. Counts toward your final assessment gate.

questions.question: Populations evolve by natural selection when there is:
options: Variation, competition, differential survival and inheritance
questions.explanation: All four ingredients are required; remove any and allele frequencies cannot shift adaptively.

questions.question: The nitrogen-fixing bacterium in bean root nodules is:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes N2 in legume nodules (mutualism). Nitrobacter nitrifies; Pseudomonas denitrifies.

questions.question: Oxygenated blood reaches the aorta from the:
questions.explanation: Left ventricle → aorta → body. (Right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs.)

questions.question: Germination requires:
questions.explanation: Water activates enzymes, oxygen fuels respiration, warmth optimises it. Light is unnecessary.

questions.question: True or False: On high power, focusing must use the fine knob only.
questions.explanation: True. Coarse moves on high power crash the lens into the slide.

questions.question: Which lose marks in examinations? (Select ALL that apply)
options: Numbering points to match the marks
questions.explanation: Vagueness, missing units and contradictions all bleed marks. Numbering points to the mark count is GOOD technique.
